h2. Problem
A comment line inside the backslash-continued {{claude \-p}} command in triage.sh ends the command early, so every first-pass triage since commit 263f5ed runs without the flags after it.
h2. Steps to reproduce
# On main, open {{desk/bin/triage.sh}} at line 140.
# Run {{shellcheck \-S warning desk/bin/triage.sh}}.
*Expected:* The triage call carries {{\-\-add\-dir $STATE}}, {{\-\-add\-dir $DESK\_SKILLS\_DIR}}, {{\-\-max\-budget\-usd}}, {{\-\-output\-format text}}, the /dev/null redirects and {{|| true}}.
*Actual:* Line 145 is a comment, so the command ends at {{\-\-permission\-mode dontAsk}}; line 146 runs as its own command and fails silently under {{|| true}}. shellcheck reports SC2215 at line 146.

h2. Diagnosis (at {{ed6401a}}, a suggestion)
* {{desk/bin/triage.sh:140\-148}}; the challenge call at {{:215\-221}} is written correctly.
* Under {{set \-euo pipefail}} (line 18), a non-zero exit from claude now aborts the script before the record check.
h2. Acceptance criteria
# AC1: Given triage.sh, when the first-pass call is built, then every flag listed under Expected reaches {{claude \-p}} (the comment moves above the command).
# AC2: Given any {{claude \-p}} call in desk/bin, when shellcheck runs at warning level, then SC2215 is not reported.
h2. Verification
* Unit: a test that stubs {{claude}} on PATH, runs triage.sh for a stub ticket and asserts the received argv contains each flag.
h2. Design
No UI.
h2. Out of scope
* Adding shellcheck to CI (DS-25).

h2. Problem
/desk-update pulls, installs and commits in the desk-skills checkout on whatever branch is checked out.
h2. Steps to reproduce
# In ~/desk-skills, check out any feature branch.
# Run /desk-update and accept a vendor upgrade.
*Expected:* It refuses to pull or install off main, and commits upgrades on a new chore/vendor-<date> branch cut from origin/main.
*Actual:* It pulls the feature branch's upstream, installs that branch's files, and commits chore(vendor) on the feature branch. On 2026-10-12 this put 8 vendor commits on fix/github-signin-session-cookies; on 2026-09-29 it left 42 vendor commits unpushed on local main, which a later PR then carried.

h2. Diagnosis (at {{ed6401a}}, a suggestion)
* {{skills/desk\-update/SKILL.md:45\-48}}: fetch and {{log HEAD..@\{u\}}} on the current branch, then {{pull \-\-ff\-only}}.
* {{skills/desk\-update/SKILL.md:140}}: commit per skill with no branch step; {{bin/skills\-upstream}} upgrade only writes vendor/.
h2. Acceptance criteria
# AC1: Given the checkout is not on the default branch, when /desk-update §1 runs, then it pulls and installs nothing and says which branch is checked out and how to switch.
# AC2: Given vendor upgrades are accepted, when §3 commits them, then they are on a new branch chore/vendor-<yyyy-mm-dd> created from origin/main, and the previous branch is untouched.
h2. Verification
* Manual: run the steps to reproduce; confirm the feature branch's log is unchanged and a chore/vendor branch holds the commits.
h2. Design
No UI.
h2. Out of scope
* Pushing and opening the PR (DS-4).

h2. Problem
Since ruleset main-protected (id 25223903) main needs a PR and a passing tests check, but /desk-update and the README still describe pushing to main.
h2. Steps to reproduce
# Run /desk-update with a vendor upgrade and accept the push.
*Expected:* It pushes the chore/vendor branch, opens a PR with {{gh pr create}}, and prints the PR URL.
*Actual:* The skill says "ask before git push" after committing on the current branch; a push to main is rejected by the ruleset.

h2. Diagnosis (at {{ed6401a}}, a suggestion)
* {{skills/desk\-update/SKILL.md:140\-141}}.
* {{README.md:510}}: "cd ~/desk-skills && git pull && ./install.sh" assumes main is checked out.
h2. Acceptance criteria
# AC1: Given committed vendor upgrades on a chore/vendor branch, when the user agrees to push, then the branch is pushed and a PR is opened and its URL reported; nothing is pushed to main.
# AC2: Given README's update section, then it says to pull on main only and that changes go through a PR.
h2. Verification
* Manual: run /desk-update against a repo with an available upgrade; confirm a PR exists and main's log is unchanged.
h2. Design
No UI.
h2. Out of scope
* Merging the PR (CI and the user do that).

*Context:* Part of the 2026-10-16 desk-skills bug sweep (parent epic). Evidence verified against main at ed6401a; transcript quotes are from past Claude Code sessions. Ben 2026-10-16: "it needs to be resolved globally so that we don't end up having multiple copies of Playwright unless there is a specific reason".

h2. Outcome
upload-images.mjs and github-signin.mjs run on one Playwright and one Chromium that desk installs, so they work in every repo (including ones with no Playwright) and never open the shared login with a different browser build.
h2. Evidence
* {{desk/bin/find\-playwright.mjs:1\-27}}: "Playwright is not ours to install: use the one this repo already has".
* Resolved 2026-10-16: pr-ninja 1.55.0, gygg-platform 1.57.0, voicepa and forewatt 1.58.2, yieldindex hoisted; pranicuk and desk-skills NOT FOUND. Four Chromium builds cached (about 2.3 GB).
* The shared profile was last written by Chrome 155; pr-ninja's 1.55 runs Chromium 140, which crashed on it on 2026-10-10 (pr-ninja config note).
* DESK\_PLAYWRIGHT set by hand in 20+ sessions: "the uploader can't find Playwright in ~/pr-ninja, and my searches for another installed copy were blocked" (pr-ninja, 2026-10-04).
h2. Acceptance criteria
# AC1: Given install.sh, when it runs, then it installs a pinned playwright version and its Chromium under {{~/.claude/desk/playwright/}} and records the version.
# AC2: Given any repo, including pranicuk and desk-skills, when upload-images.mjs or github-signin.mjs runs, then it uses desk's Playwright; DESK\_PLAYWRIGHT still overrides it.
# AC3: Given a repo's own Playwright (for its e2e tests), then desk neither uses nor changes it.
# AC4: Given /desk-update, when the pinned version changes, then install.sh installs the new one and removes Chromium builds no desk component uses any more.
h2. Verification
* Manual: in pranicuk (no Playwright) run github-signin.mjs and an upload against a draft PR; both succeed with DESK\_PLAYWRIGHT unset.
* Unit: tests/test\_playwright.mjs resolves desk's copy first.
h2. Design
No UI.
h2. Out of scope
* Claude's own browser (Playwright MCP) and the shared login (DS-6).
* Repos' e2e Playwright versions.
h2. Decisions
* 2026-10-16 Ben: desk installs its own Playwright; repos keep theirs only for their own tests. The pinned version is the one @playwright/mcp uses at the time of the PR, so both share one Chromium build.
h2. Build on
* {{desk/bin/find\-playwright.mjs}}
* {{install.sh}} Playwright MCP section (:638-760)

_Size and Launch Priority are in their fields._

*Context:* Part of the 2026-10-16 desk-skills bug sweep (parent epic). Evidence verified against main at ed6401a; transcript quotes are from past Claude Code sessions. Blocked by DS-5 (same Playwright version). Ben 2026-10-16: "lots of occasions where I end up having to sign in multiple times to GitHub".

h2. Outcome
Ben signs in to GitHub once per machine (again only when GitHub's session expires, about every two weeks), and both Claude's Playwright browser and PR image upload use that login in every repo and worktree.
h2. Evidence
* All 18 copies of the plugin's .mcp.json are unpatched: {{"args": ["@playwright/mcp@latest"]}} with no {{\-\-user\-data\-dir}}; {{install.sh:642}}: "A plugin update resets the file"; the re-patch is skipped when install.sh has no terminal (DS-10).
* With no user-data-dir the MCP uses a per-workspace profile; there are 23 mcp-chrome-* profiles in ~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright-mcp/, each needing its own sign-in.
* "Signed in and saved ... Still logged out after a restart." (pr-ninja, 2026-10-10).
h2. Acceptance criteria
# AC1: Given github-signin.mjs completes, then it saves the GitHub login as one storage-state file at a machine-level path (not a per-repo config row; the row stays as an override).
# AC2: Given the Playwright MCP server, then it is configured at user level (not by editing the plugin's .mcp.json) to run desk's pinned @playwright/mcp with {{\-\-isolated \-\-storage\-state <that file>}}.
# AC3: Given a playwright plugin update, when Claude Code restarts, then the MCP still loads the saved login (the user-level server takes precedence, or the plugin's server is disabled).
# AC4: Given a signed-in machine, when a new session in any repo or worktree opens github.com in the MCP browser, then it is signed in without a prompt.
# AC5: Given the saved login has expired, when upload-images.mjs runs, then it says the login has expired and names the sign-in command (no timeout on a missing comment box).
h2. Verification
* Manual: sign in once; open github.com via the MCP in pr-ninja, voicepa and a worktree; run an upload in pranicuk; all signed in. Run {{claude plugin update playwright}}, restart, repeat.
h2. Design
No UI.
h2. Out of scope
* Installing Playwright (DS-5).
* Logins for sites other than GitHub.
h2. Decisions
* 2026-10-16 Ben: use \-\-isolated with \-\-storage-state (documented in Playwright MCP README) rather than a shared persistent profile, which avoids profile locks between sessions and version-mismatch crashes.
* 2026-10-16 Ben: §2 browser-profile becomes a machine-level default with the per-repo row as an override.
h2. Build on
* {{desk/bin/find\-playwright.mjs}} saveSession / loadSessionCookies
* {{desk/bin/desk\-env.mjs:184,406}} browser-profile resolution

h2. Problem
The triage prompt tells the worker to run git commands its permission settings refuse, so lanes are chosen without the prior-art check and against a stale checkout.
h2. Steps to reproduce
# Run an autopilot triage on any ticket.
# Read the transcript's denied Bash calls.
*Expected:* Every command the prompt names runs under the triage settings, against an up-to-date origin/main.
*Actual:* {{git \-C <repo> ...}}, {{git ls\-tree}} and {{git fetch}} are denied: about 250 denials across 4 transcript sweeps (76 of 110 pr-ninja triage sessions 2026-10-08..16). "Permission to use Bash with command git -C /Users/benlavender/pr-ninja log \-\-oneline origin/main \-\-grep=KAN-1072 has been denied." "Your local main is far behind GitHub and doesn't contain the backfill file at all."

h2. Diagnosis (at {{ed6401a}}, a suggestion)
* {{desk/bin/worker\-settings.mjs:200\-212}}: GIT\_READ has no ls-tree; fetch is in GIT\_LOCAL, which triage denies; GIT\_DENY includes {{\-C*}}.
* triage.sh already runs from {{cd "$MAIN"}}, so {{\-C}} is unnecessary.
h2. Acceptance criteria
# AC1: Given the triage prompt, then it names commands without {{\-C}} (triage runs in the repo root) and only commands the triage settings allow.
# AC2: Given triage settings, then {{git ls\-tree}} on any ref is allowed.
# AC3: Given an autopilot batch, when triage starts, then the orchestrator has run one {{git fetch}} in the main checkout first, so triage reads a current origin/main.
# AC4: Given a test that renders the triage settings, then each command in the prompt's prior-art step matches an allow rule.
h2. Verification
* Unit: the AC4 test in tests/.
* Manual: one triage run in pr-ninja shows zero denied git calls.
h2. Design
No UI.
h2. Out of scope
* Allowing fetch inside triage (triage stays read-only).
h2. Decisions
* 2026-10-16 Ben: the orchestrator fetches once before triage; triage stays read-only.
h2. Touches
* DS-22 also edits worker-settings.mjs.

h2. Port from Sophos-Education
* Source: https://github.com/Sophos-Education/studia-skills/pull/10 (triage hardening, Sophos-Education). The triage prompt there names only allowed commands: no {{git \-C}}, {{git for\-each\-ref}} instead of {{git branch}}, no {{find}}.
* Also close {{desk/bin/worker\-settings.mjs:201}}: the allow prefix {{git branch \-r:*}} lets {{git branch \-r \-d origin/x}} through read-only triage; allow only the listing forms.

h2. Problem
The C/D lane challenge confirmed 32 of 33 times seen, several times after every code read it tried was denied, because its prompt says doubt means confirm.
h2. Steps to reproduce
# Run a challenge on a lane C ticket while its reads are denied (or read a past challenge transcript).
*Expected:* A challenger that could not check the code says so, and the plan shows the lane as unchecked.
*Actual:* "Bash was denied, so this rests on the first pass's own file references" followed by CONFIRM; one ran with its only Bash read denied and its only Read missing, then wrote {"verdict": "CONFIRM", "lane": "D"} (pr-ninja, 2026-10-08).

h2. Diagnosis (at {{ed6401a}}, a suggestion)
* Challenge prompt in {{desk/bin/triage.sh}}: "Doubt means confirm".
h2. Acceptance criteria
# AC1: Given a challenge whose code reads failed, then its verdict is INCONCLUSIVE with the reads that failed.
# AC2: Given an INCONCLUSIVE verdict, when plan-batch shows the batch, then that ticket's lane is marked unchecked and listed for the user to confirm or re-lane before it parks.
h2. Verification
* Unit: plan-batch test with an INCONCLUSIVE challenge record.
h2. Design
No UI.
h2. Out of scope

h2. Problem

# Admit ticket C while the driver runs, and let C's PR go green.

h2. Diagnosis (at {{ed6401a}}, a suggestion)
* {{desk/bin/merge\-driver.sh:53}}: {{\-\-tickets) TICKETS="$2"}}, read once.
h2. Acceptance criteria
# AC1: Given a running driver, when a ticket joins the batch in the queue, then the driver merges its PR on a later loop with no restart.
# AC2: Given desk-autopilot's instructions, then they no longer say to restart the driver after an admit.

No UI.

h2. Problem
/desk-update runs install.sh without a terminal; ten settings prompts are then skipped, but only two are offered back, so settings such as the Playwright MCP patch never get applied.
h2. Steps to reproduce
# Run {{./install.sh </dev/null}} in a context with no terminal (as /desk-update does).
# Read the summary and /desk-update's report.
*Expected:* The summary lists every skipped prompt, and /desk-update offers each one.
*Actual:* Skips print a line but are not counted; /desk-update reports the warning count and re-offers only the name-only index and the update notice. "The installer wanted to point it at the shared desk profile ... but it couldn't ask without a terminal" (2026-10-03).

h2. Diagnosis (at {{ed6401a}}, a suggestion)
* {{install.sh:117\-124}} confirm() prints "skip ..." without adding to WARNINGS; prompts at :222, :314, :454, :519, :556, :586, :615, :724, :750, :774.
* {{have\_tty}} ({{:114}}) tests /dev/tty, not stdin, so {{</dev/null}} does not force skips when a terminal exists, contrary to {{skills/desk\-update/SKILL.md:57}}.
h2. Acceptance criteria
# AC1: Given install.sh skips a prompt, then its final summary lists it under "Skipped (no terminal)" with the question.
# AC2: Given /desk-update, then for each skipped prompt it reports one SETTING row: the question and the exact command to apply it (or "run ./install.sh in a terminal").
# AC3: Given stdin is not a terminal, then install.sh treats prompts as skipped even if /dev/tty exists.
h2. Verification
* Unit: run install.sh with a temp HOME and stdin from /dev/null; assert the skipped list.
h2. Design
No UI.
h2. Out of scope
* Changing what any prompt does.

h2. Diagnosis (at {{ed6401a}}, a suggestion)
* {{skills/desk\-setup/SKILL.md:250\-251}}.
* Writers: {{desk\-pr/SKILL.md:239,269,307,318}}, {{desk\-ticket/SKILL.md:111}}; {{desk\-cleanup/SKILL.md:403}} deletes stale folders there.
h2. Acceptance criteria

# AC2: Given an existing config whose handoff directory is not writable, when /desk-setup runs, then it flags the row and re-asks it.
h2. Verification
* Manual: /desk-setup in a repo with ~/Downloads/ set flags the row.
h2. Design
No UI.
h2. Out of scope

* Session handoffs (.handoffs/ in the repo, a separate rule).
h2. Decisions
* 2026-10-16 Ben: ~/desk-handoff/ (not privacy-protected, Finder can open it, shared across repos with <TICKET>/ subfolders).

# Create a worktree with setup-worktree.sh (copies the file).

* {{skills/desk\-setup/bin/harness\-rules.py:336\-376}} cmd\_remove acts on one {{\-\-settings}} file.
* Copies: {{desk/bin/setup\-worktree.sh:105\-123}}; {{skills/desk\-setup/SKILL.md:378}}; revoke path {{:478\-480}} never mentions worktrees.

# AC1: Given a revoke, then every worktree copy (from {{git worktree list}}) that matched the main file before the revoke is updated, after a backup.

h2. Problem
A requeued ticket whose old log holds AUTOPILOT\_DONE is never respawned, and a park file from an earlier round is read as the new worker's question.
h2. Steps to reproduce
# Let a worker finish ticket K (log has AUTOPILOT\_DONE).
# Requeue K the documented way.
# Run the pass.
*Expected:* K respawns, and no old park question is shown.
*Actual:* K stays STALLED ("not respawning") until the log is moved aside by hand; a leftover parks/K.json shows yesterday's question as "needs you". "VPL-276 has sat queued for about 90 minutes without a worker being spawned" (voicepa, 2026-10-07); "That KAN-1179 alert was a false alarm ... leftover file from yesterday's park" (pr-ninja, 2026-10-16).

h2. Diagnosis (at {{ed6401a}}, a suggestion)
* {{desk/bin/pass.mjs:296\-301}} alreadyFinished() blocks on AUTOPILOT\_DONE; {{:314\-316}} reports STALLED.
* Nothing deletes parks/<KEY>.json ({{pass.mjs:335\-410}}, {{spawn\-worker.sh:45}}); {{pass.mjs:180\-186}} reads it.

h2. Problem
